full_narration: Could this jammed gear be echoing an ancient Greek computer? I grab the story, and its bronze wheels open. In 1901, divers found wreckage near Antikythera. A corroded lump concealed bronze gears. It was Greek, about two millennia old. A hand crank drove interlocking wheels. One pointer tracked the Sun. Another followed the Moon's changing phase. Rear dials counted calendar cycles. A spiral dial predicted eclipses. Another dial marked games, including the Olympics. Researchers rebuilt its hidden gearwork. That earned it the nickname ancient computer. It calculated the sky without electricity. A shipwreck preserved a machine that turned astronomy into gears.
